jobs.description:
Position Summary


The Tech Lead will coordinate and lead vulnerability management technology improvements across multiple technical teams responsible for delivering components of the end-to-end vulnerability management process.

This role will drive the transition from manually coordinated vulnerability remediation to a continuously monitored, automated, and risk-based operating model. The Tech Lead will oversee the integration of continuous monitoring, automated security testing, vulnerability intelligence, automated decisioning, patch orchestration, and remediation validation to enable vulnerabilities to be addressed at machine speed with minimal human intervention.

The role requires strong technical leadership, cross-functional coordination, experience with software development and modern engineering practices, and practical knowledge of Agile delivery using the Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe). It also requires the ability to balance automation and rapid remediation with operational resilience, compliance, security, and appropriate human oversight for high-risk or exceptional scenarios.


Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the technical delivery of vulnerability management technology improvements across multiple engineering, security, infrastructure, application, cloud, and platform teams.
  • Coordinate cross-team dependencies, priorities, risks, delivery timelines, technical decisions, and implementation activities.
  • Establish and maintain vulnerability management requirements and guide the team’s delivery of technical solutions, capabilities, architectures, implementation plans, and measurable outcomes.
  • Promote consistent engineering standards, integration patterns, automation practices, data quality, security controls, and operational processes.
  • Develop and maintain success metrics and reporting framework (e.g. roadmaps, outcomes, etc.).
  • Ensure technology enhancements support the complete vulnerability management lifecycle, including:
    • Asset and vulnerability identification
    • Continuous monitoring
    • Risk assessment and prioritization
    • Automated remediation
    • Patch testing and deployment
    • Validation and verification
    • Reporting and metrics
    • Exception and risk acceptance management
  • Oversee the seamless integration of continuous monitoring, automated security testing, vulnerability intelligence, automated patching, and remediation validation across the technology estate.
  • Oversee implementation or end-to-end, machine-driven vulnerability remediation workflows that identify, assess, prioritize, remediate, and validate vulnerabilities to ensure alignment to objectives and executive outcome drivers.
  • Coordinate the integration of security tools with:
    • Asset and configuration management platforms
    • Vulnerability scanners
    • Endpoint and patch management tools
    • CI/CD pipelines
    • Cloud platforms
    • DevOps and infrastructure automation tools
    • IT service management systems
    • Reporting and analytics platforms
  • Drive the use of APIs, orchestration, event-driven workflows, infrastructure automation, and policy-as-code to reduce manual handoffs and accelerate remediation.
  • Ensure automated patching processes include appropriate deployment safeguards, such as:
    • Deployment rings
    • Canary releases
    • Maintenance windows
    • Pre-deployment testing
    • Rollback capabilities
    • Exception handling
    • Recovery procedures
  • Collaborate with Product Owners, Enterprise and Solution Architects, Engineering Leads, Security teams, Operations teams, and other delivery stakeholders.
  • Support planning and execution within Agile SAFe ceremonies, including PI Planning, backlog refinement, sprint planning, system demos, reviews, and retrospectives.
  • Track delivery progress and proactively resolve technical issues, delivery risks, impediments, and cross-team dependencies.
  • Contribute to technical roadmaps, solution designs, estimates, business cases, investment proposals, and delivery plans.
  • Ensure solutions are scalable, secure, resilient, supportable, auditable, and aligned with enterprise architecture and cybersecurity requirements.
  • Establish measurable service-level objectives for vulnerability detection, prioritization, remediation, validation, and exception closure.
  • Monitor automation performance using metrics such as:
    • Remediation cycle time
    • Automation coverage
    • Patch success rate
    • Rollback rate
    • Validation failure rate
    • False-positive rate
    • Vulnerability recurrence rate
    • Percentage of vulnerabilities remediated without manual intervention
    • Percentage of vulnerabilities remediated within service-level objectives
  • Ensure automated actions are auditable, traceable, policy-compliant, and supported by appropriate logging, monitoring, alerting, access controls, and change records.
  • Partner with platform engineering, DevOps, infrastructure, application, cloud, and security teams to embed vulnerability remediation into development and operational workflows.
  • Lead continuous improvement initiatives to increase automation coverage, reduce remediation latency, improve data quality, and safely remove unnecessary manual intervention.
  • Communicate complex technical topics, delivery progress, risks, and recommendations clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Required Experience and Skills

  • Master's degree (or equivalent) and 15+ years of experience.
  • Must have an active Secret clearance.
  • Experience working as a Tech Lead, Technical Delivery Lead, Engineering Lead, Security Engineering Lead, or in a similar technical leadership role.
  • Demonstrated experience coordinating technology delivery across multiple technical teams and organizational boundaries.
  • Experience designing, implementing, or operating automated vulnerability remediation and patch orchestration capabilities.
  • Strong understanding of software development lifecycles, modern engineering practices, application architectures, and operational support models.
  • Practical experience working in Agile environments, preferably using the Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe).
  • Strong understanding of continuous monitoring, automated security testing, CI/CD, DevSecOps, infrastructure automation, and event-driven integration patterns.
  • Understanding of vulnerability management, cybersecurity operations, security tooling, risk management, and risk-based vulnerability prioritization.
  • Experience integrating vulnerability scanners, endpoint management platforms, configuration management tools, ticketing systems, cloud services, security platforms, and deployment pipelines.
  • Knowledge of automated patch validation, deployment safeguards, release management, rollback strategies, and recovery procedures.
  • Experience using APIs, scripting, workflow automation, orchestration platforms, policy-as-code, or similar automation technologies.
  • Ability to establish automation KPIs and use operational data to improve remediation effectiveness.
  • Ability to balance machine-speed remediation with operational resilience, security controls, compliance obligations, change management, and business continuity.
  • Experience defining governance models, approval thresholds, exception processes, and human-oversight controls for automated changes.
  • Ability to manage technical dependencies, delivery risks, competing priorities, and stakeholder expectations.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, facilitation, and influencing skills.
  • Experience leading cross-team adoption of automation and standardizing processes across diverse technology environments.
  • Ability to convert business, security, compliance, and operational requirements into actionable technical requirements and deliverable outcomes.

Desirable Qualifications and Experience

  • Experience with enterprise vulnerability management platforms and security scanning technologies.
  • Knowledge of risk-based vulnerability management, vulnerability intelligence, exploitability analysis, and exposure management.
  • Experience integrating security tools with IT service management, asset management, configuration management, cloud, DevOps, endpoint, and reporting platforms.
  • Experience with automated patching solutions and endpoint or server management technologies.
  • Familiarity with deployment rings, canary releases, blue-green deployments, automated rollback, and progressive delivery.
  • Experience embedding vulnerability remediation into software development and CI/CD pipelines.
  • Familiarity with Agile delivery tools such as Jira, Azure DevOps, or equivalent platforms.
  • Experience working in regulated, high-availability, or business-critical technology environments.
  • Knowledge of cloud security, container security, infrastructure-as-code, software composition analysis, static application security testing, and dynamic application security testing.

jobs.excerpt: Individual Giving and Donor Engagement Manager Together for Girls works around the world and combines state-of-the-art data with powerful advocacy to end violence against children and adolescents, especially sexual violence.
jobs.description:
Individual Giving and Donor Engagement Manager

Together for Girls works around the world and combines state-of-the-art data with powerful advocacy to end violence against children and adolescents, especially sexual violence. As the host of the Brave Movement, a survivor-led global advocacy initiative, we support and mobilize survivors and allies worldwide to drive political will, influence policy, and ensure that inaction is not an option.

By connecting the dots between understanding the problem, identifying effective solutions, tracking progress, and getting solutions into the hands of those with the power to make change, TfG amplifies our impact and drives toward the ultimate goal of creating a safer world for children and adolescents.

We are rooted in the conviction that violence is preventable and chance is possible, drawing upon 19 years of data from the Violence Against Children and Youth Surveys (VACS), new and emerging science, and lived experience. The Safe Futures Solutions Hub shares evidence and practice-based knowledge to inform effective prevention and response efforts, ensuring access to proven solutions across sectors. The Out of the Shadows Index tracks countries’ progress in addressing violence, providing an accountability framework and benchmark for advocacy. Brave Movement members and other activists leverage these tools to transform evidence into collective action for prevention, healing, and justice.

We are a nimble and highly impactful team that continues to grow and evolve. We work with a broad range of organizations, researchers, and advocates to drive change.

Position Overview

We are seeking an ambitious and experienced Manager, Individual Giving & Donor Engagement to join our Development team at an exciting moment in TfG’s growth. This is a rare opportunity to help shape and build an Individual Giving program from its early stages, bringing your experience, ideas and fundraising expertise to an organisation with significant potential to grow its base of individual supporters.

With the Brave Movement continuing to grow as a powerful global network of survivors, advocates and organisations, alongside TfG’s wider profile and reach, there is opportunity to build new audiences and turn growing engagement into lasting relationships with individual supporters and donors. You will have scope to test, learn and shape what Individual Giving looks like at TfG, from audience development and fundraising propositions to campaigns, digital fundraising and donor journeys.

The timing is particularly exciting. TfG is also embarking on a brand consultation, of which one key objective will be strengthening the appeal of our brand to fundraising audiences. Working closely with the Communications department and colleagues across the organization, you will have an opportunity to bring a fundraising lens to this work and help shape how TfG connects with future supporters.

Reporting to the Senior Director, Development, you will implement and help evolve TfG’s Individual Giving strategy, manage day-to-day delivery, build the individual giving pipeline, track performance against agreed KPIs, and bring insight and recommendations that help shape our wider fundraising approach. The role will also strengthen donor stewardship and engagement across the wider Development portfolio, working closely with Development colleagues, relationship owners and the Communications department.

If you are excited by the prospect of building something, rather than simply managing something that already exists, this is an opportunity to make a significant mark on TfG’s next phase of growth.

Key Responsibilities & Duties

1. Individual Giving Programme & Pipeline

  • Implement and help evolve the Individual Giving strategy, with a focus on audience growth, donor acquisition, conversion and retention.
  • Translate agreed strategy into annual individual giving plans, campaigns, fundraising propositions and donor journeys, including one-off and recurring giving.
  • Build and manage the individual supporter and donor pipeline, using CRM and audience data to segment, identify and nurture prospective donors.
  • Work with the Communications department to develop audience-building and fundraising approaches that convert engagement into individual giving.
  • Track and report on key performance indicators, including audience growth, donor acquisition, conversion, retention, income and ROI, using insights to recommend improvements.

2. Donor Engagement & Stewardship

  • Strengthen donor stewardship and engagement across the wider Development portfolio, working with relationship owners to deliver timely and consistent donor communications and touchpoints.
  • Identify opportunities to use organizational milestones, program achievements and impact stories for donor cultivation and retention.
  • Support the planning and delivery of donor cultivation events and other engagement opportunities.

3. Fundraising Communications & Content

  • Work with the Communications department to identify and develop donor-facing content and engagement opportunities that support donor cultivation and fundraising.
  • Support the development of donor-relevant stories, newsletters, digital content, pitch materials and campaign communications.

4. Project Management

  • Manage agreed individual giving and donor engagement projects from planning through delivery, coordinating timelines, milestones, inputs and follow-up.
  • Track performance, learning, risks and dependencies, escalating issues and opportunities to the Senior Director as appropriate.

Other duties, as assigned.

Desired Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

Essential

  • 4+years experience managing and growing a successful Individual Giving program within the nonprofit sector.
  • Demonstrated experience leading successful audience development, campaigns, donor journeys and/or digital fundraising.
  • Strong project management skills, with experience managing multiple priorities, deadlines, stakeholders and deliverables.
  • Strong analytical skills and confidence using data and performance indicators to inform fundraising decisions and improve activity.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to develop compelling fundraising propositions and donor-facing materials for different audiences.
  • Experience using CRM systems and donor databases to manage audiences, supporters and donor information.
  • Strong relationship-building skills and confidence working with colleagues, donors, partners and other stakeholders.
  • Ability to work collaboratively across Development, Communications and program teams.
  • Familiarity with remote-first, asynchronous working.
  • Commitment to TfG's mission and values and to survivor-centred approaches to ending violence against children and adolescents.

Highly Desirable

  • Experience with digital fundraising platforms, email marketing or online acquisition.
  • Experience working with individual philanthropists or mid-level donors.
  • Experience supporting donor events and stewardship programmes.
  • Experience working in an international nonprofit or global advocacy environment.

Location & Ways of Working

This position is a full-time position that can be based in the Washington, DC metro area. Applicants should have work authorization for their preferred location.

This is currently a remote position with the expectation to travel to attend some in-person meetings periodically. This position will also require travel up to 10%.

All team members are expected to be available during Together for Girls’ core working hours of 8:00 AM - 12:00 PM Eastern Standard Time. The other four hours that the team member chooses to work are flexible and may be coordinated with their supervisor.

Compensation

jobs.description:
Role Purpose

The Strategic Account Executive exists to drive Omilia's enterprise revenue growth in the North American market by winning and expanding high-value, strategically important accounts. The role is the primary commercial owner of a portfolio of Fortune 500 and Global 2000 target accounts, responsible for creating, advancing, and closing complex multi-stakeholder opportunities for Omilia's AI-powered contact center automation platform. Operating at the intersection of enterprise sales, executive relationship management, and solution selling, this individual brings deep credibility in the CX and conversational AI space to articulate and defend Omilia's differentiated value proposition. The Strategic Account Executive is expected to be a high-performing, self-directed revenue contributor who consistently exceeds targets and raises the commercial bar for the North American sales organization.

Accountabilities

  • Own the full enterprise sales cycle for strategic accounts in the North American market, from initial engagement through close and expansion.
  • Drive net-new revenue by acquiring and growing high-value enterprise accounts aligned with Omilia's Ideal Customer Profile across banking, healthcare, insurance, and utilities sectors.
  • Build and maintain executive-level relationships (C-suite, VP of CX, VP of IT, COO) within target accounts, positioning Omilia as the preferred AI-powered contact center automation partner.
  • Develop and execute account strategies, territory plans, and pipeline forecasts that meet or exceed quarterly and annual revenue targets.
  • Act as the primary commercial authority for your accounts, coordinating cross-functional resources — Solution Consulting, Professional Services, Customer Success, Legal — to ensure successful outcomes.
  • Represent the voice of the customer internally, contributing market and competitive intelligence to product, marketing, and leadership to influence go-to-market strategy.

Key Responsibilities

Pipeline Development & Prospecting

  • Prospect and qualify enterprise opportunities through a combination of outbound activity, partner referrals, marketing-sourced leads, and executive networking.
  • Build and maintain a self-generated pipeline of 3–4x quarterly quota coverage, with a disciplined focus on ICP accounts in banking, insurance, healthcare, and utilities.
  • Map target accounts across multiple buying centers (CX, IT, Operations, Procurement, Finance) and identify the right entry points for executive engagement.
  • Leverage intent data, industry event calendars, and partner ecosystems (system integrators, CCaaS vendors) to identify in-market opportunities at the earliest possible stage.
  • Develop and execute territory plans on a quarterly basis, aligning prospecting activity to revenue goals and reporting progress to VP of North American Enterprise Sales.

Discovery & Solution Positioning

  • Lead structured discovery engagements to diagnose prospect pain points, map decision-making structures, and define compelling business cases tied to measurable ROI.
  • Translate prospect challenges (containment rates, AHT, agent attrition, digital deflection) into quantified value narratives anchored to Omilia's platform outcomes.
  • Position Omilia's full portfolio — OCP, miniApps, Diamant, Pathfinder, CoPilot, Agentic Self-Learning — in the context of each prospect's specific automation maturity and technology stack.
  • Facilitate executive alignment sessions, including live demos, proof-of-concept scoping, and outcome-based business reviews, in partnership with Solution Consulting.
  • Identify competitive displacement opportunities where prospects are running on legacy IVR, competing conversational AI platforms, or in-house NLU builds.

Deal Execution & Stakeholder Management

  • Develop and present executive-level proposals, RFP responses, and solution overviews in collaboration with Solution Consulting and Pre-Sales Engineering.
  • Manage complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles (typically 6–18 months) involving procurement, IT, legal, compliance, and CX/operations teams.
  • Orchestrate internal deal teams — Pre-Sales, Legal, Deal Desk, Finance — to structure proposals that meet prospect requirements while protecting Omilia's margin and risk posture.
  • Navigate procurement and vendor assessment processes, including security reviews, RFP/RFI responses, and SOC 2 / HIPAA / PCI-DSS compliance questionnaires.
  • Build and maintain multi-threaded relationships at each strategic account, ensuring no deal is dependent on a single sponsor or champion.
  • Anticipate and resolve deal-level obstacles — budget cycles, internal champion transitions, competitive re-evaluations — with proactive stakeholder engagement and creative commercial structuring.

Commercial Negotiation & Contracting

  • Negotiate commercial terms, contract structures, and SLA agreements in alignment with Omilia's pricing and deal desk guidelines.
  • Structure multi-year, value-based subscription and platform agreements that align to prospect ROI expectations and Omilia's ARR growth objectives.
  • Partner with Deal Desk and Legal on Master Services Agreements, DPAs, and order forms, ensuring commercial velocity without exposing Omilia to unacceptable contractual risk.
  • Apply judgment on discounting, payment terms, and contract flexibility within approved parameters, escalating to VP-level for exceptions.

CRM Hygiene & Revenue Forecasting

  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date opportunity and account data in CRM (Salesforce), including pipeline stage, close dates, deal size, and activity logs.
  • Provide a rigorous, data-supported weekly forecast to the VP of North American Enterprise Sales, with explicit risk and upside commentary per opportunity.
  • Contribute to monthly and quarterly business reviews with pipeline trend analysis, competitive intelligence, and win/loss learnings.
  • Ensure all discovery, demo, and negotiation activity is logged in Salesforce in real time to enable accurate territory and business planning.

Customer Expansion & Retention

  • Collaborate with Customer Success and Professional Services at handoff to ensure a smooth transition and set the foundation for long-term account expansion.
  • Identify and develop upsell and cross-sell opportunities within the existing customer base, growing account ARR through adoption of additional Omilia miniApps, modules, and services.
  • Conduct periodic strategic account reviews with key customers, positioning new capabilities (Agentic Self-Learning, Pathfinder, CoPilot) as the customer's automation roadmap matures.
  • Act as executive sponsor and internal advocate for strategic accounts, ensuring post-sale commitments are met and renewal risk is identified and mitigated early.

Market Presence & Brand Representation

  • Participate in field marketing events, industry conferences (e.g., CCW, CX Summit, Money 20/20), and executive briefings to strengthen brand presence and generate pipeline.
  • Represent Omilia's thought leadership on conversational AI, CX automation, and voice biometrics in prospect and partner engagements.
  • Contribute competitive and market intelligence back to Product, Marketing, and Sales leadership to inform roadmap and go-to-market strategy.

Requirements

Knowledge, Skills & Experience

Required:

  • 7+ years of enterprise B2B SaaS sales experience, with at least 3 years in a quota-carrying role targeting Fortune 500 / Global 2000 accounts.
  • Demonstrated track record of consistently achieving or exceeding annual revenue quotas of $1M+ ARR.
  • Experience selling complex technology solutions into the contact center, CX automation, or conversational AI space is strongly preferred.
  • Expertise in enterprise sales methodologies (MEDDIC, MEDDPICC, Challenger Sale, or equivalent) and disciplined pipeline management.
  • Ability to engage and influence senior executive stakeholders (CxO, VP-level) in business-outcome-driven conversations.
  • Strong commercial acumen — ability to build and present ROI models, TCO analyses, and business cases tailored to enterprise buying committees.
  • Experience navigating complex procurement, compliance, and legal processes in regulated industries (banking, healthcare, insurance preferred).
  • Proficiency with Salesforce CRM and modern sales enablement tools (Outreach, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Gong, or equivalents).
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills; able to author compelling executive narratives and present with confidence to large audiences.
  • Self-directed and highly organized; able to manage 15–25 concurrent enterprise opportunities across multiple deal stages without sacrificing quality.
  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Technology, or a related field (or equivalent professional experience).

Nice to have:

  • Experience with AI, NLU, or speech technology platforms (e.g., Nuance, Google CCAI, AWS Connect, or similar).
  • Existing executive-level network in banking, insurance, healthcare, or utilities sectors in North America.
  • Familiarity with CCaaS platforms (Genesys, NICE, Avaya, Cisco) and how they integrate with conversational AI solutions.
  • MBA or relevant postgraduate qualification.

Omilia Note

- Contribute actively and effectively as an integrated team member.
- Act as an Omilia ambassador in all interactions.

  • Proficiency in spreadsheets and budget development tools.
  • Excellent organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple concurrent pitches and deliver accurate work within tight deadlines.
  • A collaborative, solutions-oriented mindset and the ability to work effectively across creative and commercial teams.

Open the Books is a project of American Transparency, a 501(c)(3) dedicated to educating the public on waste, fraud and abuse and fighting for real-time spending transparency. We believe transparency building block of representative government that makes all our other freedoms possible.
We operate the largest private database of public spending in history: 10 billion points of data that includes all federal salaries, line-by-line federal spending, all 50 state “checkbooks,” millions of state-level salaries and pension funds, and spending across more than 17,000 municipalities.

About the Role

A growing U.S.-based Family Law firm is seeking an experienced Senior Family Law Paralegal / Case Manager to take meaningful ownership of complex Florida family law matters.

The ideal candidate understands the full picture of each case, anticipates attorney needs, identifies potential issues, manages deadlines proactively, and helps move cases forward with strong judgment and initiative.

You will work directly with experienced attorneys and play an important role in case preparation, discovery, financial analysis, client communication, and the continued development of internal workflows and processes.

Key Responsibilities

Case Management & Attorney Support

  • Maintain a comprehensive understanding of assigned cases, including facts, procedural status, discovery, financial matters, deadlines, and outstanding needs.
  • Proactively monitor cases and identify missing information, upcoming deadlines, and potential issues.
  • Prepare attorneys for mediations, hearings, depositions, and trials.
  • Create case chronologies, issue summaries, discovery summaries, financial summaries, exhibit lists, and supporting materials.
  • Track cases from intake through resolution and ensure important deadlines and tasks are not overlooked.

Legal Document Preparation

  • Draft and prepare initial filings, pleadings, motions, notices, and other court documents.
  • Prepare and review financial affidavits and supporting documentation.
  • Assist with marital settlement agreements, parenting plans, and settlement-related documents.
  • Draft discovery requests, responses, subpoenas, deficiency correspondence, and related materials.
  • Review documents for accuracy, completeness, consistency, and attention to detail.

Financial & Discovery Review

  • Review financial affidavits, income documentation, expenses, assets, liabilities, bank records, and opposing-party disclosures.
  • Identify inconsistencies, omissions, unusual transactions, incomplete responses, and unexplained financial information.
  • Track outstanding discovery and document requests.
  • Recommend additional discovery or follow-up when information is incomplete or raises additional questions.
  • Organize complex financial information so attorneys can quickly understand the financial position of each party.

Florida Family Law & E-Filing

  • Prepare and submit documents through the Florida Courts E-Filing Portal.
  • Monitor filing acceptances, rejected filings, service requirements, and procedural follow-up.
  • Schedule hearings using applicable Florida county scheduling systems.
  • Navigate county-specific procedures, court divisions, local administrative requirements, and judicial preferences.
  • Maintain accurate and organized electronic case files.

Client & Professional Communication

  • Communicate professionally and compassionately with clients throughout sensitive family law matters.
  • Follow up with clients regarding required documents, outstanding information, deadlines, and case updates.
  • Communicate with attorneys, opposing counsel, court personnel, experts, process servers, and other legal professionals.
  • Recognize issues that require immediate attorney attention.
  • Handle confidential personal and financial information with discretion.

Technology & Workflow

  • Maintain accurate information in case-management and document-management systems.
  • Work efficiently with digital files, shared drives, electronic filing platforms, and legal technology.
  • Use Microsoft Outlook, Word, Excel, and related applications confidently.
  • Help improve internal procedures, templates, checklists, and case-management workflows.
  • Support the development and training of additional legal support team members as the practice grows.

Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years of hands-on Florida Family Law paralegal experience.
  • Experience independently managing or taking significant ownership of family law cases.
  • Strong knowledge of Florida family law procedures and documentation.
  • Demonstrated experience drafting pleadings, motions, financial affidavits, discovery, parenting plans, and settlement-related documents.
  • Strong experience reviewing financial disclosures and identifying inconsistencies or missing information.
  • Experience preparing attorneys for mediations, hearings, depositions, and/or trials.
  • Hands-on experience with the Florida Courts E-Filing Portal.
  • Experience with Florida county-specific filing and hearing scheduling procedures.
  • Strong written and verbal English communication skills.
  • Exceptional organization, attention to detail, judgment, and deadline management.
  • Ability to work independently in a remote environment while maintaining strong communication with attorneys and team members.
  • Ability to manage multiple active cases and competing priorities.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with Clio.
  • Experience with SharePoint.
  • Experience creating or improving legal procedures, templates, workflows, and checklists.
  • Previous experience training, mentoring, or supervising paralegals or legal support professionals.
  • Experience working in a growing U.S. law firm where initiative and independent judgment are highly valued.

Ideal Candidate

You are proactive, detail-oriented, and confident taking ownership of your cases.

You do not wait to be told what needs attention. You review the file, understand the objective, identify what is missing, and communicate clear recommendations to the attorney.

You are comfortable working independently while remaining collaborative and responsive. You understand that Family Law requires both strong technical skills and emotional intelligence, and you can communicate professionally and compassionately with clients experiencing difficult personal situations.

Why Join This Opportunity?

  • 100% Remote: Work remotely while supporting an established U.S. Family Law practice.
  • Senior-Level Responsibility: Become deeply involved in case preparation and strategy rather than performing only administrative tasks.
  • Direct Attorney Interaction: Work closely with experienced attorneys and contribute meaningfully to case progress.

Job Description

End User Technical Support & Issue Resolution

Nuestra Compañía – Plukon Food Group

Plukon Food Group es una multinacional europea líder en el sector alimentario que colabora con socios de la cadena para ofrecer una amplia gama de productos, incluidos componentes de comidas, ensaladas y proteínas vegetales alternativas.

Estamos presentes en 7 países (Países Bajos, Bélgica, Alemania, Polonia, Dinamarca, Francia y España), con 44 sedes y 12.000 empleados.
Nos enfocamos en ofrecer alimentos responsables producidos de manera sostenible, cuidando del bienestar animal, del medio ambiente y de las personas.

Puesto: Technical Application & Integration Support Engineer

¿Te gusta resolver retos técnicos complejos relacionados con aplicaciones, integraciones, bases de datos y APIs?

Como Technical Application & Integration Support Engineer, tendrás un papel clave para garantizar el correcto funcionamiento de Poultry Master en las diferentes operaciones europeas. Investigarás incidencias técnicas, darás soporte a las integraciones, contribuirás a mejorar los procesos de CI/CD y ayudarás a reforzar una plataforma esencial para el negocio.

¿Quieres formar parte de un entorno IT internacional y tener un impacto real? ¡Únete a Plukon!

Funciones

Como Technical Application & Integration Support Engineer, te encargarás de garantizar que Poultry Master y los sistemas conectados funcionen de forma fiable y eficiente en toda la organización.

  • Proporcionar soporte técnico para Poultry Master y sus integraciones con sistemas internos y externos.

  • Investigar incidencias relacionadas con aplicaciones, integraciones, bases de datos e infraestructura para identificar la causa raíz e implementar soluciones.

  • Analizar bases de datos PostgreSQL, validar la calidad de los datos y resolver inconsistencias mediante técnicas avanzadas de SQL.

  • Dar soporte y resolver incidencias relacionadas con APIs, integraciones e intercambio de datos entre aplicaciones.

  • Colaborar en la gestión de repositorios de GitHub, procesos de CI/CD y despliegues.

  • Aprender y dar soporte a las configuraciones técnicas de la plataforma low-code Rappit.

  • Coordinar investigaciones técnicas con los equipos internos de IT y documentar las soluciones a incidencias recurrentes.

  • Identificar mejoras estructurales que aumenten la estabilidad de la plataforma y la eficiencia operativa.

Esto es lo que hacemos juntos

En Plukon trabajamos cada día para ofrecer soluciones de alimentación responsable en toda Europa. Combinamos nuestra experiencia internacional con una cultura práctica y cercana, en la que las personas asumen responsabilidades y trabajan juntas para conseguir resultados.

Te incorporarás al equipo de Poultry Master, dentro de IT Software Support, y colaborarás estrechamente con compañeros de Países Bajos y otros países europeos.

Se trata de una posición en remoto, con viajes ocasionales a Países Bajos.

¿Qué buscamos?

  • Experiencia profesional en soporte de aplicaciones, APIs, integraciones o entornos técnicos de software.

  • Conocimientos sólidos de PostgreSQL y SQL, incluyendo consultas complejas y conceptos de bases de datos relacionales.

  • Experiencia con APIs REST, JSON y resolución de incidencias relacionadas con integraciones entre sistemas.

  • Experiencia práctica con Git y GitHub y conocimientos de procesos CI/CD.

  • Capacidad de análisis y resolución de problemas, buenas habilidades de comunicación y nivel fluido de inglés.

¿Qué ofrecemos?

Te incorporarás a una organización que apuesta por ser un buen lugar para trabajar, fomentar una comunicación abierta y apoyar el desarrollo de las personas.

Además, ofrecemos:

  • Un puesto internacional, trabajando con compañeros y diferentes interlocutores de toda Europa.

  • La oportunidad de trabajar con una plataforma clave para el negocio y utilizada en distintas operaciones.

  • Flexibilidad para trabajar en remoto desde Europa.

  • Oportunidades de desarrollo en soporte de aplicaciones, integraciones y tecnologías de plataforma.

  • Un entorno colaborativo donde se valoran la iniciativa, la autonomía y la mejora continua.

    Así puedes seguir creciendo

    ¿Quieres seguir aprendiendo o asumir nuevas responsabilidades? En Plukon tendrás espacio para hacerlo. Tu crecimiento empieza con tu propia iniciativa.

    En este puesto podrás ampliar tus conocimientos en arquitectura de aplicaciones, PostgreSQL, integraciones, CI/CD y plataformas low-code. Tendrás la oportunidad de desarrollar nuevas competencias técnicas, contribuir a la mejora de la plataforma y trabajar con compañeros de diferentes países y áreas.

    Piensa global. Actúa local. Haz que suceda.

    ¿Te ves trabajando como Technical Application & Integration Support Engineer en Plukon?

    Entonces, inscríbete.

Company Description

The International Fresh Produce Association (IFPA) is the largest global organization serving the fresh produce and floral supply chain. With a mission to unite the industry, IFPA drives innovation and collaboration to create a vibrant future for all its members. The association provides value through advocacy, connecting members, and offering actionable guidance to support industry prosperity. IFPA is dedicated to empowering businesses and professionals across the supply chain to succeed with confidence and purpose.

Position Summary

The Director, Events is responsible for leading a team of professional event managers and coordinating and overseeing the planning, budgeting, execution, and evaluation of the International Fresh Produce Association’s events. This includes the annual Global Produce and Floral Show, and a portfolio of international events in regions/markets around the world. These events are among IFPA’s primary means of engaging members, delivering valuable insights, networking, and business connections for members across the fresh produce and floral supply chains, from farm to retail, and growing their prosperity. The Director, Events works closely with the Chief Strategy and Programs Officer to:

  • Create innovative, engaging experiences that attract and deliver value to a diverse mix of global attendees
  • Enhance global member engagement, recruitment, and retention
  • Drive IFPA revenue growth
  • Manage event professionals and collaborate with colleagues across business units of IFPA to coordinate and execute the events.

Position Responsibilities

Leadership & Management (30%)

  1. Provide leadership that models and promotes performance-based strategy and values-based culture.
  2. Actively and routinely solicit and provide input on strategic and tactical decision-making to achieve IFPA goals.
  3. Provide strategic direction and oversight to member volunteer committees and purpose-driven task forces, as appropriate.
  4. Lead, coach and develop a high-performing team of events professionals.
  5. Manage staff performance and provide coaching and onboarding, to foster a culture of innovation and promote a member-focused approach to event and program design and execution.
  6. Develop, implement, and continuously improve event operations standards, policies, procedures, and best practices to ensure consistency, efficiency, risk mitigation, knowledge transfer, and operational excellence across IFPA’s event portfolio.

Event Development, Direction, and Evaluation (35%)

  1. Lead the development, design, execution, and evaluation of a comprehensive event portfolio strategy long-term sustainability and financial growth. Manage event revenue, create and communicate financial projections for event budgets.
  2. Collaborate with and coordinate internal and external partnerships that leverage shared interests, resources, and mutual benefit. Collaborate with IFPA colleagues and partners to develop business cases and recommendations for event investments, enhancements, and growth initiatives.
  3. Serve as a staff liaison for appropriate committee(s) related to events. Participate in cross-functional teams and task forces as needed.
  1. Collaborate with the Director, Trade Show in ongoing evaluation of programs and management of annual business planning and budgets.
  1. Identify, introduce, and use business processes and systems that support efficient, effective, and high-caliber performance.

Event Management (30%)

  1. Provide oversight for the planning and execution of IFPA Events, including the Global Produce and Floral Show, applying events planning and management skills to enhance member experience and grow participation in the events, support membership retention efforts and promote year-round value that drives membership.
  2. Develop, implement, and evaluate event planning to optimize member value and revenue opportunities. Oversee development and execution of all event-related projects and customer service.
  3. Manage all onsite operations of designated events.
  4. Oversee venue selection strategy, contract negotiations, and operational partnerships for the Global Produce and Floral Show.
  5. Collaborate with VP, Member Engagement and Business Development, Sales Team and Sponsorship Fulfillment Manager to identify new revenue-driving opportunities and set pricing to deliver member value and support IFPA financial growth.

Professional Development (5%)

  1. Expand business and personal competencies by attending professional meetings, workshops, and seminars.
  2. Actively participate in IFPA staff meetings, committees, and purpose-driven task forces.
  3. Be up to date on and apply research concerning industry trends, members’ needs and interests, and topics relevant to this role.
  4. Participate in strategic initiatives related to ongoing evaluation, evolution and design of IFPA expos and events.

Miscellaneous Position Information

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

  1. Bachelor’s Degree in Event Management, Planning, Project Management or related field or equivalent work experience. CAE and/or CMP desirable.
  2. 7+ years of progressively responsible experience in leading large-scale conferences, tradeshows, and event porfolios, including budget oversight, staff management, and strategic planning responsibilities.
  3. 7+ years of experience leading and developing professional staff.
  4. Proficient computer skills such as Microsoft Word, Excel, event management systems, Zoom, Teams and a working knowledge of database programs such as Sales Force.
  5. Able to work independently as well as in a team setting, be flexible, agile, and meet deadlines.
  6. Excellent interpersonal communications and presentation skills.
  7. Strong analytical and budget management skills.

Measures for Success

  1. Meets or exceeds annual event net revenue targets.
  2. Effective team building: Develop and maintain strong relationships with teams by effectively leading, motivating and communicating with direct reports and team members (measured by member and team feedback).
  3. Events meet key objectives for member engagement and satisfaction as well as IFPA revenue goals.
  4. Innovation and expansion of events and strategic projects.

If you are looking for a new opportunity to grow with a clinician founded and clinician led organization, look no further! Hospitals, community clinics, investment bank funded group practice startups, state agencies, and more.

At OptiMindHealth, we continuously strive to provide consistent, high-quality care and expand the reach of mental health care services in our communities. Unfortunately, the need often outpaces the services available to those we serve and only adds to the current mental health crisis in our nation. To combat this crisis and further our mission, we need more compassionate and skilled clinicians to join our cause. We are not interested in the “burnt-out” clinician that no longer finds meaning in their work and is just going through the motions; we are seeking people with a passion to provide excellent care, and the belief that we, together, can make a difference. If that’s you, then you’re in the right place!

Our approach with our team is simple, we take care of you, the clinician, so you can take care of patients. How do we do that? By investing in your growth, supporting you financially, holistically, and professionally, while being flexible regarding your personal needs and goals. The work we do with patients is hard enough and over the years we have found that our team often does their best work when the administrative burdens are taken off their plate and they are able to be fully present with their patients. Our administrative support team handles all non-clinical tasks so that you don’t have to think about anything except focusing on your patients.

Why bother with the endless administrative burdens and isolation of private practice? Use your highly trained interpersonal skills to change the culture around mental health care, decrease stigma, and help people who need you, while being supported by an experienced multi-disciplinary team of clinicians. Let us take care of the rest!

Want to work part time? No problem. Want to do group therapy? Sure! Want to do long-term psychodynamic psychotherapy with all of your clients? We do it every day. Interested in treating couples? We can make that happen. Basically, what we are saying is that whatever outpatient care you are interested in providing, we can surely accommodate you. We know you have exceptional skills; we want you to be part of our team.

The perfect candidate will share our passion for improving and expanding access to high quality mental health care and will thrive in a culture that emphasizes creativity, authenticity, humor, compassion, acceptance, and determination. Telehealth or onsite, we support your authentic and unique growth trajectory, while being yourself and having some fun!

We prioritize the clinician's experience by offering excellent compensation, benefits, training/supervision, and flexibility. Whether you’re working from home or in one of our physical offices, if you’re doing it during your scheduled work hours, you’re getting paid for it. Our compensation packages include:

  • Health care benefits.
  • Generous paid vacation and sick leave time.
  • Paid administrative time for consultation, supervision, and documentation.
  • Full administrative support.

  • Paid supervision, clinical rounds, and administrative time.
  • Customized schedules within available clinic hours.
  • Hybrid work environment if desired: Telehealth and/or in-person (in select locations).
  • Muti-disciplinary team approach to treatment.
  • Incredible administrative support team.
  • Company leadership that understands the practice of mental healthcare.
  • Inclusive, socially responsible, client focused leadership.
  • We are not a franchise or a big investor-backed company.
  • And most importantly, clinician-led and clinician-FOCUSED!

We know what it’s like to work in an organization led by businesspeople instead of clinicians. We, on the other hand, have organically grown as a socially responsible company that started as a single provider on a mission to destigmatize and broaden the reach of mental health care, to an integrated and holistic group of exceptional providers with diverse backgrounds working toward that mission. We are fortunate to have significantly increased the reach of mental health care services in our communities, and look forward to continuing to provide consistent, high-quality care to those we serve for many years to come.

  • Proven experience owning production services, managing service-level agreements, monitoring platform performance, and leading incident response and resolution activities.
  • Working knowledge of cloud networking concepts, including API routing, service endpoints, encryption in transit, and cloud connectivity.
  • Understanding of identity federation, OAuth 2.0, SAML, and zero-trust security principles within cloud environments.
  • Familiarity with cloud-native service operations, API governance, event-driven architectures, and service dependency management.

Salesforce Marketing Automation Consultant

Marketing Automation | Remote, India | Full-Time | APAC

Bluprintx (BPX) is a global, AI-powered consultancy built to design and deliver the intelligent front office for CMO and CRO executives. We are private equity-backed and scaling fast, with 300 active customers across 10 countries and more than 1,750 implementations. We connect people, technology, and AI to turn fragmentation into performance, partnering with global leaders to modernize how marketing, CRM, content, AI & Data connect. At BPX, we hire operators and specialists who thrive at the intersection of commercial strategy and technical execution.

What We Do: Cutting Complexity Across the Front Office

We help the world's most ambitious companies, including Uber Eats, BNY, and Xerox, untangle the operational complexity that slows enterprise growth. As a Gold Adobe Solution Partner and Salesforce Summit Partner, we deliver strategy and implementation across the full front office. Our proprietary methodology builds sustainable enabled ecosystems that maximize ROI and accelerate speed to market. By embedding AI into commercial workflows, we help clients move faster and stay ahead.

The Role

A hands-on Salesforce Marketing Cloud (SFMC) consultant who owns day-to-day campaign execution. Time is split between BAU campaigns and proactive platform for a key client and backlog work for the internal team across SFMC and Marketo. Senior Consultants set strategy and handle escalations. This role takes real ownership of daily builds and client communication, working proactively rather than waiting for tickets. Ability to cross train into Marketo and / or other platforms with support is highly desirable.

What you'll do

  • Client support: own everyday SFMC execution for a dedicated client, including email builds, audience segmentation and campaign launches.
  • Email production: build clean, responsive emails from scratch and adapt code from the existing template library.
  • Personalisation and journeys: set up dynamic content with AMPscript and manage automated flows in Journey Builder and Automation Studio.
  • Data and segmentation: write basic-to-intermediate SQL queries to pull and manage subscriber lists including ongoing contact management and remediation.
  • Team backlog: pick up broader marketing automation requests across SFMC and Marketo, including light Marketo work (smart lists, filter logic).
  • Client engagement: speak directly with client stakeholders to keep builds moving and give clear status updates.

What you'll bring

  • 4–5 years' marketing automation experience, with practical SFMC use across Journey Builder, Automation Studio, Email Studio and Data Extensions.
  • Mid-level AMPscript: pulling personalisation from data schemas (complex SSJS and nested joins not required).
  • Solid HTML/CSS email coding, for new templates and updates to existing ones.
  • Comfortable writing basic SQL to segment audiences. Solution Architects handle heavy data modelling.
  • Clear, direct written and spoken English for everyday client updates.
  • A people person who builds relationships and engages confidently with clients.
  • Desirable: Baseline Marketo knowledge, or a quick-learning mindset for list management and filter logic.

Why this role, why now

You get your own SFMC client from day one, with the builds and the client conversations yours to run. The team backlog spans SFMC and Marketo, so you can add a second platform with support behind you while BPX scales across 10 countries.

DevSecOps Engineering

    • Drive security automation initiatives to reduce manual effort and accelerate secure software delivery.
    • Document and verify the existing security mitigations and identify if additional mitigations are required for our products.
    • Work with product development teams to guide mitigation development.
    • Contribute to the development and implementation of security tests and verification protocols. Assist in conducting security verification and validation efforts.

Product Security

  • Collaborate with product, development, and cloud engineering teams to embed security requirements throughout the SDLC.

Engineering & Collaboration

    • Continuously evaluate new tools, technologies, and approaches to improve security effectiveness and developer experience.

Required Qualifications

    • 3+ years of software development, automation, or scripting experience using Python, PowerShell, Bash, or equivalent languages.
    • Experience integrating security tooling into CI/CD pipelines, including SAST, DAST, SCA, container scanning, and secrets management.
    • Working knowledge of cloud security principles and services in Azure and/or AWS.
    • Understanding of containerized environments and Kubernetes security concepts.
    • Experience collaborating with engineering teams in Agile development environments.
    • Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills.

jobs.excerpt: JOB TITLE: General Counsel POSITION CLASSIFICATION: Vice President or Senior Vice President REPORTS TO: President & CEO LOCATION: Hybrid or Remote with a willingness to work ET hours when necessary About American Rivers American Rivers is a national conservation organization working to make every river clean and healthy for people and wildlife.
jobs.description:
JOB TITLE: General Counsel

POSITION CLASSIFICATION: Vice President or Senior Vice President

REPORTS TO: President & CEO
LOCATION: Hybrid or Remote with a willingness to work ET hours when necessary

About American Rivers

American Rivers is a national conservation organization working to make every river clean and healthy for people and wildlife. We combine evidence-based solutions with enduring partnerships to safeguard the 4.4 million miles of rivers and streams that are essential to our nation’s clean drinking water, extraordinary wildlife, and the strength of our communities. For more than 50 years, our staff, supporters, and partners have been driven by a common belief: Life Depends on Rivers.

The beauty of rivers is that they connect all people and communities – including within our organization. The life experiences, knowledge, innovation, and talent that different people bring to our work provides perspectives, experiences, and competencies which are critical to our effectiveness in protecting wild rivers, restoring damaged rivers, and conserving clean water for people and nature.

JOB SUMMARY

The General Counsel leads the organization’s legal function and heads up the legal team to provide legal services to American Rivers across a broad range of matters, including transactional and procurement agreements, employment law, nonprofit corporate governance and tax compliance, federal and state government funding compliance, intellectual property, lobbying disclosure compliance, corporate sponsorship, and charitable solicitation regulation. Serving as a member of the Executive Leadership Team (ELT), the General Counsel directs and manages all aspects of legal services for a national nonprofit organization and affiliated organizations that include a 501 (c)(4) and connected PAC in a period of growth and evolving organizational needs.

The General Counsel also advises the People and Culture Department on employment-related policies, employee benefits, insurance, and personnel matters. In addition, the General Counsel serves as a legal advisor to and partner with the executive team, staffs the Board Litigation Committee, and serves as the Board Assistant Secretary. The position oversees a legal department of four and two to four summer law clerks and reports to the Senior Vice President for Business Strategy & Operations.

PRINCIPAL RESPONSIBILITIES:

Transactional and Compliance

  • Draft and review contracts and other legal agreements, including master agreements, subgrants, corporate arrangements, memoranda of understanding, and leases, and advise staff on related compliance matters.
  • Develop, maintain, and oversee contracts tracking and approval process; monitor and report on metrics; and recommend improvements to procurement policies and procedures as needed.
  • Partner with program staff on the development and execution of RFPs and RFQs, and identify, manage, and escalate the legal issues arising for projects contracting, permitting, procurement, insurance, compliance, claims, and dispute resolution.

Corporate Governance and Tax Compliance

  • With the CEO, review and revise bylaws and other corporate documents, support sound corporate governance practices, and help maintain American Rivers’ good standing with federal and state regulators.
  • Advise staff to ensure compliance with IRS guidelines related to lobbying activities by nonprofit organizations.
  • Advise staff on state regulations applicable to charitable solicitation and assist with charitable watchdog reports as needed.
  • Advise staff on 501(c)(4) organizational compliance and program.

Risk Management

  • Develop and implement a proactive risk management framework, identify and escalate emerging legal, operational, and compliance risks to leadership, and recommend practical mitigation strategies.
  • Lead efforts to reduce liability risk by developing and reviewing internal policies and procedures.
  • Address personnel issues in ways that minimize risk and reduce the likelihood of litigation.
  • If in aggregate beneficial to American Rivers, recommend transferring risk contractually to protect the organization from undue legal exposure.
  • Oversee the organization’s insurance program, including applications, renewals, coverage questions, risk escalation, and integration of insurance requirements into contracts.

People and Culture

  • Advise and manage employment matters in close partnership with the People and Culture leader, including high-priority personnel issues.
  • Support People and Culture in ensuring compliance with applicable employment laws.
  • Establish systems and processes with People and Culture to support best practices in performance management.
  • Develop and communicate policies and procedures related to standards of legal and ethical conduct.
  • Advise on the internship programs for other departments throughout the organization.
  • Manage the annual conflict-of-interest acknowledgment for staff and board directors, as well as the disclosure process.
  • Lead recruitment, interviewing, and supervision for the legal department's summer internship program (including legal clerkships) and externships, maintaining and strengthening a rigorous program that develops emerging attorneys while benefiting the organization.

Executive and Board Relations (for both American Rivers and American Rivers Action Fund)

  • Advise the Board of Directors, President & CEO, and senior management on corporate governance, legal and regulatory compliance, risk management, and other issues affecting operations.
  • Participate as a member of key leadership teams, contributing to management and strategic planning and providing legal advice as needed.
  • Advise the Executive Office Manager and Board Liaison as needed in governance-related areas.
  • Serve as Assistant Secretary to maintain the adequacy of corporate minutes and records.
  • Staff the Board Litigation Committee to support review and oversight of organizational litigation and serve as a liaison between the Board and staff.
  • Advise and participate in board meetings.

Counsel

  • Advise staff in headquarters and field offices on organizational legal issues, litigation matters, and other matters across a range of legal practice areas.
  • As prioritized and requested by management, provide legal advice on trademark and copyright matters, secure and defend national trademarks, copyrights, and branding assets, coordinating with pro bono counsel as necessary.
  • Identify and prepare all-staff training on legal issues relevant to the organization.
  • Oversee outside counsel strategy and engagement, including matter scoping, budget management, performance oversight, and coordination to ensure timely, practical, and cost-effective legal support.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

  • J.D. and at least 15 years of successful legal practice experience.
  • Bar admission and good standing in at least one U.S. jurisdiction.
  • Prior experience as a senior attorney, preferably including General Counsel experience, with a broad legal portfolio and staff management responsibilities.
  • Collaborative approach with the ability to work effectively with multiple internal departments, external parties, and members of the Board.
  • Experience reviewing, drafting, and negotiating a variety of transactional agreements.
  • Knowledge of labor and employment law.
  • Knowledge of the OMB Guidance for Federal Financial Assistance.
  • Knowledge of intellectual property and charitable solicitation laws.
  • Experience overseeing key elements of organizational risk assessment and management.
  • Experience with cost-effective management of outside legal resources.
  • Working knowledge of federal tax and election laws as they apply to 501(c)(3), 501(c)(4), and Section 527 organizations in general and public-interest law firms in particular.
  • Experience overseeing a corporate insurance program, or knowledge of insurance law.
  • Ability to travel to board meetings and other convenings as required.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Knowledge of non-profit corporate law, specifically in the conservation sector.
  • Experience with large construction projects and related
  • Experience working on matters of corporate
  • Experience in analyzing and addressing legal ethics
  • Knowledge of federal, state, and local lobbying
  • Non-profit experience required, although it can be through pro bono
  • Familiarity with or willingness to learn our suite of tools, including Slack, Zoom, Box, Monday.com, Intacct, and the Microsoft Suite or similar tools.
  • Knowledge of or interest in environmental law and policy matters.

Candidates who are unsure if they meet all minimum qualifications or who have transferable skills and experience beyond the conservation sector are encouraged to apply.

LOCATION

Hybrid or Remote with a willingness to work ET hours when necessary.

COMPENSATION

American Rivers offers marketable compensation that reflects the qualifications and experience of the selected candidate. The salary range for this position is $181,000-$250,000 annually, depending on experience and qualifications. We provide a comprehensive Total Rewards package to our full-time, regular employees, including:

  • Health and Wellness: Medical, dental, vision, long-term and short-term disability, and life insurance.
  • Financial Security: After one year of service, American Rivers begins contributing a 3% employer contribution. There is no vesting schedule for employer contributions as employees are 100% vested upon participation.
  • Time Off: Four weeks of paid leave, eleven paid holidays, three floating holidays, and sick leave.

At American Rivers, we are committed to supporting our employee’s well-being, professional growth, and financial security, ensuring they can thrive both at work and in life.

COMMUNITY AND OPPORTUNITY

  • At American Rivers, our core values drive everything we do – we Lead with Collaboration and Trust, Infuse Equity and Justice, Deliver Results, and Ensure Staff and Volunteers Thrive. We are committed to fostering a workplace where employees feel valued, supported, and empowered to make a difference.
  • Our culture prioritizes work-life thriving through Focus Fridays (no internal meetings), professional development opportunities, a home office stipend, and our comprehensive leave policies, including sabbatical leave (every seven years) and paid parental leave (six weeks w/ one year of service).
  • We also ensure leadership stays connected to staff needs through an internal advisory group, fostering open communication and continuous improvement.
  • At American Rivers, our people are our strength, and we are dedicated to building a thriving, inclusive workplace where everyone can grow and contribute to our mission.

American Rivers is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities upon request. To request this document in an alternative format or a reasonable accommodation, please contact the Human Resources department at 202-243-7040 or . Please note that one week’s advance notice is preferred.

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States.American Rivers is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

We encourage candidates of all personal and professional backgrounds to apply.

Psychiatric Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP-BC) $135k - $160k/year

Position Requirement: Full-Time

FLSA Status: Exempt

Location: Lynnfield, Massachusetts

Salary:

135K - 160K+

Work from Home! Competitive, negotiable salary! Work/life balance! Leadership and advancement opportunities!

Join a leading clinician-led behavioral health company today! OptiMindHealth (OMH) is expanding and seeking compassionate psychotherapists to join our team. Today, OMH provides superior behavioral health services patients in Massachusetts and Colorado. Since 2016, we’ve specialized in serving both adult and adolescent patients in a supportive outpatient environment. Our practice strives to improve access to holistic and cost-effective mental health care while supporting our clinical staff in all aspects of their work. Our clinicians define this work as the perfect balance between flexibility and efficiency.

OMH offers a variety of part-time and/or full-time options to our clinicians. Packages can be customized towards every clinician’s needs. Packages can include some combination of:

· Competitive Salary

· Medical benefits

· Paid malpractice policy

· CEU reimbursement

· Paid time off (PTO) and paid holidays

· Productivity Bonuses in select areas

· Work-Life Balance

· Flexible Work Schedule

  • No extra on call work, simply cover the care for your own patients!

It is common for clinicians to diversify their work today. Therefore, OMH’s flexibility and part-time options are the perfect complement to your professional and/or personal commitments. You can feel secure that OMH will offer steady, consistent income throughout your tenure.

Work from or close to home:

With locations in Colorado and Massachusetts, OMH is continuing to expand into states around the country. OMH will work with you to identify the best “fit” and will provide everything you need to treat OMH patients remotely from the comfort of your home. Our interview process focuses on your skill sets, interest as well as geographic location to match you to the best available option to begin working with OMH. Ask to speak with our recruitment team today to identify the local office(s) in your area, as well as those offices that are being planned for launch. Of course, if you prefer to work from home, we also have fully remote positions available.

Responsibilities:

The Psychiatric Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP-BC) will participate in the integrated care team model at OMH. Outpatient behavioral health practices like OMH are getting more attention than ever before due to the emphasis on team approaches. Join OMH to perfect your skills in the emerging field of integrated behavioral health care. The interdisciplinary health care team includes physicians, psychiatric nurse practitioners, licensed clinical psychologists, and licensed mental health professionals (LICSW/LPC/LMFT/LMHP). OMH values clinical relationships between all provider levels and believes this coordinated, collaborative approach provides the highest level of care to the patients we are privileged to serve.

Customize the care for each patient:

Our clinicians have the unique ability to customize the care for each and every individual patient. You will have the autonomy to determine how often you see a patient as well as the appropriate length of time spent with each patient. Medication management and individual psychotherapy are the most common forms of clinical work performed at OMH, but our clinicians also perform family therapy, group therapy, and psychological testing as needed and/or appropriate to a wide range of presenting problems of our patients.

Pick your own schedule!

  • Enjoy the freedom to create your own custom schedules with the perfect work/life balance.
  • Typically, clinicians work between Mondays – Fridays somewhere between the hours of 7:00 AM – 7:00 PM.

Focus on the patient’s care without the hassle or any additional on-call responsibilities. Simply cover the care for you own patients! Our medical staff and clinical psychotherapists focus on the patient’s care and our back-office support team handles the rest. This allows our clinicians time to be spent where it should be; with the patients they serve. Each clinician is responsible for clinical care and documentation following treatment sessions. Once that’s complete, our support team will handle all billing, collections, credentialing, etc. Once you leave the office for the day, your time is yours. No additional on-call responsibilities and no time spent wasted dealing with insurance companies.

Interested in benefits?

Full-time clinicians are eligible to medical health benefits. Please speak with the recruitment team to obtain additional specifics on benefits.

Leadership & Advancement:

OMH is a growing, clinician-led company. Our Site Supervisors are geographically dispersed throughout the areas we work in order to have staff leaders available to every clinician. Talk with our recruitment team today about the advancement opportunities to become senior psychotherapists and/or site supervisors.

Licensure, Education & Experience:                                    

Licensure in Massachusetts as a Psychiatric Nurse Practitioner with experience working with persons who have various behavioral health issues such as, mood disorders, anxiety disorders, personality disorders, substance misuse, and other psychiatric impairments under the supervision of a consulting psychiatrist(s).  We welcome new graduates!

Preferred: Successful completion of PMHNP-BC exam(s).

This document represents the major duties, responsibilities, and authorities of this job, and is not intended to be a complete list of all tasks and functions. Other duties may be assigned as well. 

Salary: $135,000 – $160,000 / year

jobs.description:
Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist (LMFT) $62K-80K/yr

Position Requirement: Remote Full-Time and Part-time Positions Available

If you are looking for a new opportunity to grow with a clinician founded and clinician led organization, look no further! As an authentic, unique, and skilled counselor, you have a plethora of options when it comes to work. Hospitals, community clinics, investment bank funded group practice startups, state agencies, and more.

At OptiMindHealth, we continuously strive to provide consistent, high-quality care and expand the reach of mental health care services in our communities. Unfortunately, the need often outpaces the services available to those we serve and only adds to the current mental health crisis in our nation. To combat this crisis and further our mission, we need more compassionate and skilled clinicians to join our cause. We are not interested in the “burnt-out” clinician that no longer finds meaning in their work and is just going through the motions; we are seeking people with a passion to provide excellent care, and the belief that we, together, can make a difference. If that’s you, then you’re in the right place!

Our approach with our team is simple, we take care of you, the clinician, so you can take care of patients. How do we do that? By investing in your growth, supporting you financially, holistically, and professionally, while being flexible regarding your personal needs and goals. The work we do with patients is hard enough and over the years we have found that our team often does their best work when the administrative burdens are taken off their plate and they are able to be fully present with their patients. Our administrative support team handles all non-clinical tasks so that you don’t have to think about anything except focusing on your patients.

Why bother with the endless administrative burdens and isolation of private practice? Use your highly trained interpersonal skills to change the culture around mental health care, decrease stigma, and help people who need you, while being supported by an experienced multi-disciplinary team of clinicians. Let us take care of the rest!

Want to work part time? No problem. Want to do group therapy? Sure! Want to do long-term psychodynamic psychotherapy with all of your clients? We do it every day. Interested in treating couples? We can make that happen. Basically, what we are saying is that whatever outpatient care you are interested in providing, we can surely accommodate you. We know you have exceptional skills; we want you to be part of our team.

The perfect candidate will share our passion for improving and expanding access to high quality mental health care and will thrive in a culture that emphasizes creativity, authenticity, humor, compassion, acceptance, and determination. Telehealth or onsite, we support your authentic and unique growth trajectory, while being yourself and having some fun!

We prioritize the clinician's experience by offering excellent compensation, benefits, training/supervision, and flexibility. Whether you’re working from home or in one of our physical offices, if you’re doing it during your scheduled work hours, you’re getting paid for it. Our compensation packages include:

  • Starting Salary range: $62,000.00 - $80,000.00 per year.
  • 401K with maximum employee matching.
  • Health care benefits.
  • Generous paid vacation and sick leave time.
  • Paid administrative time for consultation, supervision, and documentation.
  • Full administrative support.

Here are a few extra perks our team loves:

  • Paid supervision, clinical rounds, and administrative time.
  • Customized schedules within available clinic hours.
  • Hybrid work environment if desired: Telehealth and/or in-person (in select locations).
  • Muti-disciplinary team approach to treatment.
  • Incredible administrative support team.
  • Company leadership that understands the practice of mental healthcare.
  • Inclusive, socially responsible, client focused leadership.
  • We are not a franchise or a big investor-backed company.
  • And most importantly, clinician-led and clinician-FOCUSED!

We know what it’s like to work in an organization led by businesspeople instead of clinicians. We, on the other hand, have organically grown as a socially responsible company that started as a single provider on a mission to destigmatize and broaden the reach of mental health care, to an integrated and holistic group of exceptional providers with diverse backgrounds working toward that mission. We are fortunate to have significantly increased the reach of mental health care services in our communities, and look forward to continuing to provide consistent, high-quality care to those we serve for many years to come.

We will rely on your expertise to:

  • Evaluate mental health conditions, diagnose, create, and implement a treatment plan, complete ongoing documentation including further diagnosis, treatment plan reviews, and case notes according to company policy.
  • Provide excellent care for clients and collaborate with a dynamic team to further the mission of filling gaps in our community.
  • Utilize creativity in interventions to help clients achieve and exceed goals.
  • Prepare and submit individual documentation for each session per company guidelines and protocol. 
  • For Full-Time status, clinicians must maintain at least 32 available hours for patient care per week.
  • Coordinate services with other care providers, families, work personnel, medical personnel, other OptiMindHealth staff, and school staff as needed.
  • Attend and participate in all clinical staff meetings and trainings.

Qualifications and Skill for This Positions: 

  • Master's degree in one of the behavioral sciences or related fields from an accredited college/university.
  • Full, current, unrestricted license to practice independently (LPC, LCSW, LMFT) is required.
  • Experience with electronic health records and completing clinical documentation.
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills.
  • Experience and willingness to work collaboratively and creatively to meet necessary deadlines.
  • Comfort and familiarity working with clients with a diverse range of problems or concerns. 
  • Ability to pass a background check in a way that confirms to us you can provide safe care.  
  • Demonstrate and model stable and appropriate boundaries with clients.

Additionally Valuable (but not essential) Qualifications for This Position: 

  • Experience working in community, group, or private practice mental health.
  • Currently paneled or credentialed with insurance network.
  • Multilingual or bilingual proficiency.
  • Specialty area of practice. 

We can’t wait to hear your story and look forward to sharing ours!

They represent typical elements and criteria considered necessary to perform the job successfully. The job’s responsibilities/tasks may be modified and/or expanded over time.
