Title: Research / Senior Research Manager, Weather Data Systems (Weather Initiative)

Location: India (remote). Candidates must have existing authorization to work in India; PxD is unable to sponsor visas for this role.
Salary: Salary will be competitive and commensurate with the candidate's skills, experience, and the local labor market in India

Position: Full-time

Application deadline: October 25, 2026 (applications may be reviewed as they are submitted)

About the Role:

Precision Development (PxD) is seeking a dynamic, creative, and self-motivated Research / Senior Research Manager, Weather Data Systems to join a high-performing team in India working on our weather initiative - a high-profile, fast-growing area of PxD's work with significant potential for impact and visibility.

In this role, you will help design, test, evaluate, and scale evidence-based weather solutions for smallholder farmers, working closely with researchers, government partners, and cross-functional teams. We're looking for a proactive self-starter with strong research management skills, excellent stakeholder engagement abilities, and a passion for generating actionable evidence to improve program outcomes.

While anchored in research and iterative learning, the role will work fluidly across programmatic, service delivery, and research functions - ensuring insights are embedded into program implementation, operational decision-making, and government-facing engagements.

We're hiring for this role at either the Research Manager or Senior Research Manager level. The specific level will be determined based on the candidate's years of experience, demonstrated seniority, and scope of past responsibilities.

This role suits someone who understands both the research side (what makes a forecast actionable) and the technical side (how to build a system that reliably gets it there), and who wants to build infrastructure rather than run a single one-off analysis.

Responsibilities:

  • Work with forecast science, technology, and dissemination teams to design and oversee a pipeline that converts real-time scientific forecast data into location-specific farmer messages automatically
  • Design the pipeline to be so it is adaptable to different dissemination vendors and channels (voice, SMS, WhatsApp, apps, LLM-powered advisory systems, or combinations), accommodating how each system ingests data.
  • Ensure fast, error-free delivery of time-sensitive forecast information to farmers by minimizing latencies in data transformations or other aspects of the pipeline.
  • Own the technical and process requirements for making the pipeline replicable across geographies, rather than custom-built for a single location or use case
  • Translate scientific forecast outputs and technical system constraints for research and program teams, and vice versa, so each side understands what the other needs
  • Oversee data management, quality checks, and testing of the pipeline as it scales
  • Document the pipeline's architecture, decision logic, and rationale so it can be maintained, audited, and extended by others
  • Coordinate with dissemination teams to ensure automated messages meet the standards developed by the field research team
  • Guide teams on data quality and technical rigor as the pipeline scales to new use cases or geographies
  • Provide guidance to Associate and Manager level staff supporting the pipeline
  • Contribute to funding proposals and reports on the technical build
  • Contribute to PxD's institutional knowledge management on weather data systems

What You’ll Bring:

  • Degree in a technical, quantitative, or data-related field (computer science, data science, engineering, statistics, or similar); economics or agricultural economics backgrounds with strong technical skills also considered
  • Experience building or managing a data pipeline, ideally one involving real-time or automated data processing
  • Working knowledge of the tools and languages needed to build and maintain such a pipeline (e.g., Python, SQL, or similar)
  • Ability to work across technical and non-technical teams, translating between forecast science, engineering, and program needs
  • Experience designing systems meant to be replicated or scaled, not just built once
  • Strong documentation habits: the ability to make a technical system legible to people who didn't build it
  • Strong writing and oral communication skills in English

About Precision Development (PxD):

PxD is a rapidly scaling global nonprofit working with governments across Africa and Asia to close the last-mile gap in smallholder farming. We deliver evidence-based information and tools - from timely farming and weather guidance to climate-resilient inputs - that millions of farmers use to improve their lives. In the last 12 months alone, we reached over 60 million farmers at a cost of just $0.47 per farmer per year, with our flagship program in India delivering a benefit-cost ratio of 12:1–19:1.

Operating in Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Kenya, Nigeria, and beyond, the majority of our team is based in our program countries, working directly alongside government partners and farming communities toward our goal of improving the lives of 100 million farmers by 2030.

How to Apply:

To apply, please visit the PxD website and complete the online application form, including your CV, cover letter, and brief responses to the screening questions. Applications may be reviewed as they are submitted, up until the application deadline of October 25, 2026, 5pm IST.

In line with our values, we evaluate candidates on merit alone, without regard to gender, gender identity, ethnicity, religion, disability, caste, or any other characteristic protected under applicable law. We offer flexible working arrangements to support your wellbeing. Personal data provided is used for recruitment purposes only.

Senior Technical Account Manager working from the UK.

Life is short. Work somewhere awesome.

Flare is a breakout cybersecurity Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) company with a mission to empower organizations to take control of their data and protect their customers, employees and brand by shedding light on external threats. We enable cybersecurity teams to proactively detect high-risk external exposure across the dark and clear web, before threat actors have a chance to leverage it. We unify the core functionalities of cyber threat intelligence and external attack surface management into a single, intuitive platform.

TL;DR: We are a bunch of geeks who help protect our clients' data (and people in their network) by locating cyber risks.

The Sr. Technical Account Manager (TAM) serves as a dedicated technical point of contact for customers, providing in-depth knowledge and expertise to optimize their use of the Flare platform.

In this role, you are responsible for handling the technical aspects of customer relationships, providing onboarding support, ongoing threat intelligence support, educating customers about the Flare platform, ensuring the alignment of technical solutions with customer needs, and collaborating closely with internal teams to resolve complex challenges.

Your purpose and impact:

Your mission, should you choose to accept it, is to directly and indirectly enable customers to obtain full value from their investment in Flare.

  • Act as a customer advisor, providing deep technical guidance on leveraging the Flare platform to maximize and optimize the impact of customers’ cyber threat intelligence workflows.
    • Collaborate closely with Customer Success Managers to ensure customer needs are met and aligned with their business goals.
    • Contribute to the enablement of customers on the platform and on continuous threat intelligence practices.
    • Optimize platform configurations through tuning, best practices, and hands-on guidance to ensure maximum value; including integrations using APIs, webhooks and basic scripting.
  • Manage escalations of complex technical issues and work directly with Product and Engineering teams to resolve them.
  • Use Flare to perform custom reporting on behalf of customers.
  • Develop playbooks and best practices for use by peers, customers and CS team members,
  • Participate in on-site customer visits and industry events to provide hands-on support and build strong customer relationships.
  • Provide input to the Product team on feature requests, technical challenges, and areas for improvement based on customer feedback.

You’ll be a perfect fit if you have:

  • 7+ years of experience in cybersecurity consulting, SOC analyst roles or threat intelligence roles.
  • Prior experience in threat analyst roles or with threat intelligence solutions (preferred).
  • Prior experience working in B2B SaaS environments or implementing SaaS solutions.
  • Experience working with API integrations and webhooks.
  • Basic Python development skills.
  • Excellent problem-solving skills with the ability to navigate complex technical issues and provide effective solutions.
  • Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, capable of simplifying complex technical concepts for customers.
  • Ability to work cross-functionally with CSMs, Product, and Engineering teams.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple accounts, prioritize tasks effectively and drive issues to resolution.
  • Bilingual abilities in French and English (preferred).
  • Client-facing experience.

What this role will achieve …

Within 30 Days

  • You will be deeply familiar with Flare’s platform, datasets, and customer use-cases. You will be able to perform a highly competent end to end demo of the platform to both technical and executive audiences.
  • You will have learned Flare’s systems, processes and documentation and be able to independently find answers to technical questions.
  • You will have a working understanding of TAM responsibilities, processes and work assignments.
  • You will have become familiar with Flare’s research and thought leadership and have recommended at least one article to share with a specific customer demographic, including its relevance

Within 60 Days

  • You will have completed hands-on training with the Support team, answering progressively more complicated tickets.
  • You will be able to quickly assess client deployments and recommend configuration improvements based on desired use case and best practices.
  • You will have completed at least one bespoke risk report for a customer.
  • You will have mastered several Flare integrations to be able to enable customers to integrate Flare data easily into their security program.
  • You will routinely participate in internal meetings with the Customer Success, Support and TAM teams; improving team understanding and alignment.

Within 90 Days

  • You will have helped two highly sophisticated customers unlock new use-cases and integrate Flare data into security workflows.
  • You will have developed one playbook on Flare practices and trained the Customer Success team on delivery.
  • You will routinely participate in cross functional meetings; representing customers and the broader customer facing teams.
  • You will have become an active participant in one of Flare’s continuous improvement initiatives.
  • You will be able to answer complex product questions asked by the CS and AE teams.

What it’s like to be part of Flare:

  • You will find a people-first company where work-life balance is valued. You’ll receive:
    • Competitive salary
    • Bonus structure
    • Stock options
    • Health coverage/insurance
    • Flexible, work from anywhere
    • Unlimited vacation
    • Fun company events; “Flamping”, curling, rock climbing and many others
  • You will join a high-growth, innovative start up where you’ll see your impact immediately and be empowered to take on challenges for your personal and professional growth
  • You will work with an inspiring and award-winning team who are passionate about what they do and the clients we serve, whose work has been referenced in leading academic journals and international media

Don’t meet every single requirement? Studies have shown that women and people of color are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single qualification. At Flare we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive and authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyways. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

BigCommerce is building a new team to deliver a suite of conversational AI agents spanning the B2B commerce lifecycle — Product Discovery, Pricing & Quoting, Order Automation, Fulfillment & Delivery, and Post-Sale Support. The agents are built in Go on Google ADK with Gemini, with evaluation infrastructure in Braintrust and a streaming AG-UI frontend.


As a Senior Backend Engineer specializing in AI agents, you will design the agents themselves: orchestration, sub-agent architecture, tool integration, prompt engineering, and — critically — the evaluation discipline that determines whether these agents are trustworthy enough to ship. Agent quality in this domain is won on evals, not just code, and you will own that practice for the team.


BigCommerce, part of the Commerce brand family, helps merchants increase sales at every stage of their growth. From small startups to mid-market businesses and large enterprises, we provide the leading e-commerce platform. Our customers can then concentrate on what's most important: growing their businesses. We enable our customers to build, innovate, and grow, collectively reshaping the e-commerce industry.


What You’ll Do


  • Design, build, and iterate on AI agents in Go/Python using an orchestrator/sub-agent architecture, covering intent interpretation, delegation, and safe action execution
  • Own eval-driven development: build and maintain golden datasets, scorers, and regression suites (Braintrust or similar) for critical quality metrics such as discovery recall and quote accuracy
  • Develop and refine prompts, model configurations; treat prompts and model settings as versioned, tested artifacts
  • Integrate agents with MCP servers and backend tools, defining safe tool-call contracts, approval flows for write actions, and guardrails against prompt injection and abuse
  • Instrument agents with tracing, metrics, and cost tracking; use production signals to drive quality improvements
  • Collaborate with product designers and frontend engineers to deliver intuitive, useful conversational experiences

  • Strong and proven development skills in any major language (Go/Python/Ruby/PHP)
  • Experience working with LLMs (Gemini, Anthropic, OpenAI, etc.) in production systems
  • Experience with LLM evaluation: building datasets, defining scorers/metrics, and using eval results to drive iteration
  • Strong understanding of prompt engineering, tool/function calling, and agent orchestration patterns
  • Deep experience designing and building APIs (gRPC, GraphQL, REST) and integrating data across systems
  • Hands-on experience building MCP servers or LLM tool integrations
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and ability to work in a fast-paced, exploratory environment
  • Strong collaboration and communication skills in cross-functional teams
  • Strong preference toward execution and delivery

Preferred:


  • Experience with agent frameworks (Google ADK, LangChain/LangGraph, Semantic Kernel, or similar)
  • Experience with evaluation/observability platforms (Braintrust, LangSmith, or similar)
  • Experience with RAG systems and retrieval quality tuning
  • Experience with e-commerce platforms or SaaS product development
  • Background in conversational AI or natural language processing

jobs.description:
Your Future Evolves Here

Evolent partners with health plans and providers to achieve better outcomes for people with most complex and costly health conditions. Working across specialties and primary care, we seek to connect the pieces of fragmented health care system and ensure people get the same level of care and compassion we would want for our loved ones.

Evolent employees enjoy work/life balance, the flexibility to suit their work to their lives, and autonomy they need to get things done. We believe that people do their best work when they're supported to live their best lives, and when they feel welcome to bring their whole selves to work. That's one reason why diversity and inclusion are core to our business.

Join Evolent for the mission. Stay for the culture.

What You’ll Be Doing:

Job Summary

The ERP & People Systems Architect is the design authority for Evolent's finance and people systems and their move to a headless, AI-enabled application experience where employees ask agents for HR and finance outcomes instead of navigating screens. Behind it, Workday HCM and Financials, Adaptive Planning, VNDLY, Salesforce CRM, and their payroll, benefits, banking, tax, identity, and data integrations remain the trusted systems of record. This role is a hands-on individual contributor who defines target-state architecture, technical standards, reusable patterns, and architecture decisions, and validates them through proofs of concept before teams build.

The Architect partners with the Director across all aspects of delivery, including building, operating, and automating solutions. The Architect owns architectural integrity and design quality, while the Director and delivery leaders remain accountable for priorities, capacity, and execution. The Architect also works closely with Enterprise Architecture, Analytics, Security, Engineering, Finance, Talent, and business stakeholders.


Work Location: This is a remote position. Candidates should be able to work primarily during Eastern Time business hours.


Essential Functions

  • Define the target-state architecture for the ERP and people systems portfolio and its connected systems, and sequence it into technical roadmaps with transition states, dependencies, and retirement steps, setting the major platform roadmap jointly with the Director, ERP & People Systems Delivery.
  • Decide whether needs are met through configuration, integration, or extension—delivered capabilities first, then APIs and integration tools, then custom extensions—and record significant decisions with options, trade-offs, and rationale.
  • Publish standards, reference architectures, and reusable patterns, and scale review to risk: standard changes proceed on approved patterns; new integrations, security domains, Extend apps, and external data flows receive design review; and the Architect leads design of new modules, middleware, AI agents, and major Finance or HCM redesigns with delivery and business owners.
  • Own the integration architecture and inventory for Workday and connected systems, including each integration's purpose, data, owner, security, and pattern; choose API, event, or batch patterns; set boundaries among Workday Orchestrate, Studio, EIB, and middleware; standardize authentication and error handling; and rationalize redundant point-to-point integrations.
  • Define system-of-record boundaries and data ownership for worker, organization, and finance data, including how Workday, as the authoritative worker record, feeds identity and access processes; set standards for data movement, lineage, and reconciliation; and design reporting and analytics architecture across Workday reporting, Adaptive Planning, enterprise data platforms, and business intelligence tools with Data teams.
  • Design ERP security architecture—security-group and role design, domain and business-process security, segregation of duties, privileged access, and integration identities—with controls that produce SOX and audit evidence under policies set by Security.
  • Set cloud SaaS standards for tenant and environment strategy, protection of sensitive data in non-production tenants, and resilience to vendor release changes; assess Workday's semiannual releases, vendor roadmaps, new modules, and build-versus-buy options for fit, security, supportability, and total cost through Evolent's technology review process.
  • Design the AI-enabled headless ERP experience: expose capabilities as governed APIs, events, and agent tools; keep business rules in the system of record; and decide what runs natively, in Orchestrate, or in cross-system flows built by the workplace AI and automation team.
  • Define responsible-AI requirements for AI features and agents that act on financial and people data: grounding in authoritative data, least-privilege access, human approval for transactions, evaluation and prompt-injection testing before release, cost per outcome, and audit evidence for Evolent's AI governance and Security reviews.
  • Build proofs of concept and reference implementations—API and integration prototypes, SQL data-validation queries, and agent or workflow prototypes—to test technical hypotheses, measure results, and recommend whether to adopt, extend, or stop before delivery teams commit.
  • Specify nonfunctional requirements for performance, resilience, observability (logging, alerting, reconciliation checks), and testability, including which critical business processes and integrations need automated regression coverage; delivery teams choose test tooling and run pipelines and releases.
  • Identify, classify, and size technical debt across architecture, security, integrations, and data models, including obsolete Studio integrations, and recommend a remediation sequence; delivery leaders own remediation, and the Senior Director sets investment priority.

Required Qualifications

  • 10+ years of experience in enterprise applications, ERP, or solution architecture, including architecture responsibility for business-critical finance or people systems.
  • Deep, hands-on expertise in Workday —depth in Financials or HCM and working knowledge of the other—covering business-process and security configuration, reporting, integration frameworks, tenant strategy, and release cycles.
  • Hands-on integration design across REST and SOAP APIs, event-driven and batch patterns, and tools such as Workday EIB, Studio, and Orchestrate or their equivalents, including authentication, error handling, and monitoring.
  • Strong SQL and data-modeling skills, with experience designing data flows, lineage, and reconciliation between operational systems, data platforms, and reporting or business intelligence tools.
  • Working knowledge of internal controls and privacy for financial and people data, including role-based access, segregation of duties, and SOX or comparable audit requirements.
  • Experience designing automation or AI-enabled solutions for enterprise business processes, including human-approval points, data-access controls, and governance.
  • Ability to produce architecture artifacts: current- and target-state diagrams, integration and data-flow designs, security models, decision records, and nonfunctional requirements.
  • Ability to explain architecture trade-offs in cost, risk, control, and user impact to Finance and Talent leaders and technical teams, in writing and in design reviews.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Architecture experience across both Workday HCM and Financials, and with Adaptive Planning, VNDLY, or Salesforce CRM.
  • Experience with Workday's embedded AI and agent capabilities.
  • Python or similar scripting for prototypes, data validation, or automation, using source control and deployment pipelines.
  • Experience defining evaluation, prompt-injection testing, observability, and cost controls for production AI agents.
  • Experience with Microsoft Power BI, integration platforms, or identity integrations with Microsoft Entra ID or Active Directory.
  • Experience as the architect on an ERP implementation, major module expansion, or integration modernization.
  • Experience in healthcare or another regulated industry, including HITRUST or comparable control frameworks.

Preferred Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Business, or a related field.

Preferred Certifications

  • Workday Pro certifications
  • Enterprise, cloud, integration, data, security, or AI architecture certifications.

General Performance Criteria

As the ERP Architect, you will be required to fulfill your responsibilities while meeting the following general performance criteria for this position at this level:

Expertise: Maintain hands-on depth in Workday, integrations, data, security, and AI, and keep standards current with each vendor release. Ground recommendations in tested evidence rather than assumptions.

Communication: Write decisions and designs that delivery teams can build from without rework, and explain options to business leaders in terms they can act on.

Domain: Understand how Finance and Talent processes, data, and controls work at Evolent, including close and planning cycles, payroll, compensation, and procurement, and make cross-domain trade-offs visible instead of favoring one function.

System: Be accountable for the architectural integrity of ERP and people systems, demonstrated by fewer point-to-point integrations, wider reuse of approved patterns, security-design compliance, and retired technical debt; delivery leaders own service operations and release outcomes.

Process: Keep architecture from slowing delivery: make timely decisions, drop reviews that add no value, and turn production incidents and defect trends into better standards.

Influence: Earn adoption of standards and patterns from delivery teams, peer architects, and business owners through evidence and clear reasoning rather than authority over their work.

To ensure a secure hiring process we have implemented several identity verification steps, including submission of a government issued photo ID. We conduct identity verification during interviews, and final interviews may require onsite attendance. All candidates must complete a comprehensive background check, in-person I-9 verification, and may be subject to drug screening prior to employment. The use of artificial intelligence tools during interviews is prohibited and monitored. Misrepresentation will result in immediate disqualification from consideration.

Technical Requirements:

We require that all employees have the following technical capability at their home: High speed internet over 10 Mbps and, specifically for all call center employees, the ability to plug in directly to the home internet router.

jobs.title: Single Audit Resolution Manager
jobs.excerpt: Kearney and Company is currently seeking a Single Audit Resolution Manager to join our team supporting HHS in the review, analysis, tracking, and resolution of Single Audit findings associated with federal financial assistance programs.
jobs.description:
Kearney and Company is currently seeking a Single Audit Resolution Manager to join our team supporting HHS in the review, analysis, tracking, and resolution of Single Audit findings associated with federal financial assistance programs. The individual will work closely with federal program, grants management, audit resolution, and financial management stakeholders to evaluate audit findings, assess recipient corrective actions, support management decisions, and help ensure identified deficiencies are appropriately resolved. The role requires a strong understanding of federal grants management, Single Audit requirements, internal controls, and audit resolution processes, as well as the ability to analyze complex audit information and communicate recommendations clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  • Review Single Audit reports, findings, questioned costs, corrective action plans, and related recipient documentation.
  • Analyze audit findings to determine applicable federal requirements, underlying control deficiencies, and actions necessary to support resolution.
  • Support HHS officials in evaluating the adequacy of recipient corrective actions and determining whether findings have been sufficiently addressed.
  • Assist with the development, documentation, and tracking of management decisions and other audit resolution actions.
  • Monitor open audit findings and corrective actions through resolution, including aging, recurring findings, outstanding documentation, and follow-up requirements.
  • Identify repeat or systemic findings across recipients, programs, fiscal years, or compliance requirements and elevate potential areas of risk.
  • Perform research and analysis related to federal grant requirements, Single Audit requirements, program-specific requirements, and applicable HHS policies and procedures.
  • Coordinate with grants management officials, program offices, financial management personnel, auditors, recipients, and other stakeholders to obtain information necessary to resolve findings.
  • Review recipient responses and supporting documentation to determine whether corrective actions appropriately address identified deficiencies.
  • Assist in evaluating and documenting the disposition of questioned costs and other monetary findings.
  • Maintain accurate and complete audit resolution records, supporting documentation, status information, and audit trails.
  • Develop reports, dashboards, briefings, and other management information regarding the status and trends of Single Audit findings.
  • Support analysis of Single Audit data to identify recurring internal control weaknesses, compliance issues, emerging risks, and opportunities to strengthen federal oversight.
  • Recommend improvements to audit resolution processes, workflows, tracking mechanisms, data quality, and internal controls.
  • Support the development of standard operating procedures, job aids, templates, and other resources to promote consistent audit resolution practices across HHS.
  • Participate in meetings with federal stakeholders and provide clear summaries of outstanding issues, required actions, risks, and recommended next steps.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, business administration, public administration, auditing, or a related field.
  • Minimum of 5 years of experience supporting federal or state and local grants management, audit resolution, financial management, compliance, or program integrity activities.
  • Working knowledge of the Single Audit process and federal financial assistance requirements, including 2 CFR Part 200.
  • Experience with federal grants administration, post-award monitoring, or oversight of recipients and subrecipients.
  • Familiarity with the Federal Audit Clearinghouse (FAC) and Single Audit reporting data.
  • Experience reviewing or preparing management decisions, corrective action determinations, questioned cost dispositions, or audit follow-up documentation.
  • Experience reviewing audit findings, internal control deficiencies, corrective action plans, or similar compliance documentation.
  • Ability to interpret federal regulations, policies, audit documentation, and program requirements and apply them to specific findings or circumstances.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to evaluate complex information, identify underlying issues, and develop well-supported onclusions and recommendations.
  • Strong written communication skills, including the ability to prepare concise analyses, decision documentation, reports, and executive-level summaries.
  • Strong organizational and project management skills with the ability to manage multiple findings, deadlines, stakeholders, and follow-up activities simultaneously.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Teams.
  • Ability to work collaboratively with federal clients, auditors, program officials, grants management professionals, and other stakeholders.
  • Ability to work independently, exercise sound professional judgment, and identify issues requiring escalation or additional review.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance (requires U.S. Citizenship).

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Direct experience supporting Single Audit resolution for a federal agency, particularly HHS or an HHS Operating or Staff Division.
  • Knowledge of the Uniform Guidance Single Audit requirements under 2 CFR Part 200, Subpart F.
  • Understanding of federal internal control, improper payment, fraud risk management, or program integrity concepts.
  • Experience identifying recurring or systemic issues across multiple audit findings, recipients, programs, or fiscal years.
  • Experience using data analytics, dashboards, or reporting tools to track audit findings, corrective actions, and resolution performance.
  • Experience with Power BI, Tableau, Python, or other data analysis and visualization tools.
  • Experience developing or improving audit resolution workflows, standard operating procedures, controls, or case management processes.
  • Certified Public Accountant (CPA), Certified Internal Auditor (CIA), Certified Government Financial Manager (CGFM), Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE), or other relevant professional certification.
  • Prior experience working with HHS grants, financial assistance programs, or HHS grants management and oversight processes.

Overview

Exclusively focused on the Government, Kearney & Company provides financial services, including auditing, consulting, and technology services. Our commitment to our employees and clients as well as to dedication and trust, critical values to our Firm, have led to Kearney’s recognition as one of the leading accounting firms in the country. Based on our employees’ feedback, we are also consistently rated a Best Place to Work. Employment at Kearney means a flexible, collaborative, and open-minded work environment. We hope it is your “first easy decision.” Learn more at www.kearneyco.com/careers." ,"

The expected salary range for this position is between $77,000 and $125,000. This range is representative of base pay only and does not include straight time pay for hours worked over 40 per week, company contributions towards paid benefits, and/or bonuses.  Actual compensation (meeting or exceeding the range) will bedeterminedbased on specific experience, education, work location, clearance level, and other factorspermittedby law.  This position is eligible for bonuses (when applicable). 

  

We also offer a competitive benefits package that includes:
